title: What are Flexible Constructor Bodies (JEP 513: statements before super()/this()), and why do they enable safer validation/initialization?
keyPoints: JEP 513 allows statements before super() or this() calls in constructors
Previously super() had to be the very first statement, preventing pre-validation
Now you can validate parameters, compute values, and log before calling the parent constructor
The prologue cannot access this (the object is not yet initialized) but can work with parameters
Enables fail-fast validation: throw IllegalArgumentException before constructing a partially invalid object
Eliminates the need for static helper methods to validate constructor arguments

s1_definition.oneliner: Flexible Constructor Bodies allow statements before super() or this(), enabling parameter validation and computation before the parent constructor runs.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Before JEP 513** – `super()` or `this()` had to be the first statement in a constructor; any validation or computation had to happen after or via static helper methods.
- **After JEP 513** – statements can appear before the `super()` or `this()` call, forming a "prologue" that validates inputs, computes derived values, or logs.
- **Restriction** – the prologue cannot access `this` (the object is not yet initialized), so it can only work with constructor parameters and local variables.
- **Benefit** – fail-fast validation: reject invalid arguments before any object construction begins.
s1_definition.analogy: Before, when opening a new bank account (calling super()), you had to start immediately with no pre-checks. After JEP 513, you can verify the customer's ID, validate the opening balance, and check branch eligibility before the account is created. If validation fails, no account object ever exists.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Constructor Execution Order:

  BEFORE JEP 513:
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ super(id, balance);          │ ◀── must be first
  │ if (balance < 0) throw IAE;  │ ◀── too late! super already ran
  └──────────────────────────────┘

  AFTER JEP 513:
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ if (balance < 0) throw IAE;  │ ◀── prologue: validates first
  │ balance = round(balance);    │ ◀── compute derived value
  │ super(id, balance);          │ ◀── safe: validated + computed
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Flexible Constructor Bodies (JEP 513, Java 24 preview) allow statements before super() or this() in constructors. Previously, Java required super() as the first statement, forcing validation to happen after the parent constructor had already run with potentially invalid arguments.

Now you can validate parameters, compute derived values, and fail fast before any object construction begins. A `SavingsAccount` constructor can reject a negative opening balance before `super()` ever runs, ensuring no partially constructed invalid object exists.

The prologue cannot access `this` (the object is not yet initialized), so it works only with constructor parameters and local variables. This covers the vast majority of validation needs. For complex logic, call static helper methods from the prologue.

Remember one sentence: flexible constructor bodies allow validation before super(), enabling fail-fast rejection of invalid arguments before any object is constructed.
